newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: NATCHICKS IN BOTSWANA BROILER VENTURE.
newsitem.headline: NATCHICKS IN BOTSWANA BROILER VENTURE.

text.p: Botswana's Associated Investment Development Corporation (AIDC) and South Africa's National Chicken Farms on Monday announced a partnership aimed at making Botswana self sufficient in day-old broler chicks by early 1998.
The venture, known as National Chicks Botswana (NCB), opened a five million pula factory on Sunday night.
NCB has three incubators installed and it is hoped that it will be able to replace half of Botswana's chicken imports almost immediately.
Between 175,000 and 200,000 day-old broilers are imported from Zimbabwe and South Africa weekly.
By February next year, when two further incubators are installed, the factory is expected to be able to replace all of the country's imports.
The operation is expected to save the country eight million pula in foreign exchange and create 25 new direct jobs and up to 1,000 in the broader industry.
AIDC is an operation of Botswana businessman Satar Dada, while NatChicks is listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
